outcome: Polignac's conjecture is not settled. Since 26 January 2024 the bounded-gap constant H1 (the least gap that recurs infinitely often) has been pushed from 246 to 240 (Stadlmann, arXiv, 31 Aug 2026, unconditional), 236 (Song and Yue, IACR ePrint 2026/1893, Sept 2026, unconditional per abstract), 212 (Charton, Ono and co-authors with Axiom Math, preprint, 3 Sep 2026) and 186 (OpenAI, 'GPT-6 Astra', preprint, Aug–Sep 2026, conditional on three explicit inputs). Each shows that some even gap up to H1 recurs infinitely often, not which gap, and none shows every even gap does. Several unrefereed claims of the full conjecture or of its twin-prime case appeared in the same period (Zenodo Jan and June 2026, MUSTIC 2024/2025, a 2024 journal paper, and an arXiv line of work whose Polignac claim was dropped from the abstract in Aug 2026); I found no expert acceptance of any of them.
problem_asks: (1) A universal claim over every positive even integer n (infinitely many even n, not a single n). (2) For each such n: infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes p < q with q - p = n, i.e. infinitely many prime gaps of size n. Equivalently: the set of even 'Polignac numbers' (even n occurring as a consecutive-prime gap infinitely often) is all of 2N. The statement contains the twin prime conjecture as its n = 2 case and the cousin prime case n = 4. It does not ask for a bound on the least such n, for a density, or for counts of gaps; those are neighbouring quantities. Note that the statement concerns consecutive primes; the 'weak' Polignac numbers (even numbers that are differences of two primes in infinitely many ways) are a different set.

events.what_happened: Yitang Zhang announced on 17 April 2013 a proof that infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes differ by at most 70,000,000 (H1 <= 7x10^7). Accepted by Annals of Mathematics in early May 2013 (per Wikipedia); published Annals 179(3) (2014) 1121-1174.
events.revisions: Journal version Annals 179 (2014).
events.delivers: Unconditionally, some even gap d <= 7x10^7 recurs infinitely often (finite H1). No specific d is identified.
events.remains: The all-even-n claim: which even gaps recur is not determined beyond the existence of one below 7x10^7.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication in early May 2013 (per Wikipedia); published 2014

events.direction: Partial: supports that some bounded even gap recurs infinitely often; says nothing about any named even n.

events.what_happened: Janos Pintz, arXiv:1305.6289 (27 May 2013): separates strong Polignac numbers (even gaps occurring infinitely often between consecutive primes) from weak ones. Hanson's 2015 paper (arXiv:1501.06690) describes Pintz as proving the Polignac numbers have positive lower density, with an ineffective constant; the abstract I opened does not state that density claim, and I did not read the full text. A 2016 book-chapter version exists per a search listing (not opened).
events.revisions: Book chapter (Springer, 2016) per search listing, not opened.
events.delivers: Positive lower density of the set of strong Polignac numbers, per secondary description. This is a statement about how many even numbers are Polignac, not that all are.
events.remains: Membership of each even n. The statement that every even n is a Polignac number.
events.direction: Partial, toward density of the Polignac set; does not identify which even n are Polignac.

events.what_happened: Baoshan Zhang, arXiv:1306.0795 (4 Jun 2013; v2 11 Jun 2013), 'Matrix Online Characteristic Number and its applications in Goldbach Conjecture, Polignac Conjecture, the Twin Prime Conjecture'. Abstract says the author proves infinitely many odd primes are separated by four (the n = 4 case, Theorem 9), gives a conditional result for gap 2m (Theorem 11), and 'prove[s] that there are an infinite number of twin prime'.
events.revisions: v2 11 Jun 2013 (per listing).
events.delivers: Claims the n = 2 (twin) and n = 4 (cousin) cases. The conditional gap-2m statement is conditional on a hypothesis stated in the abstract. If the claims held they would settle those two cases only.
events.remains: Every other even n, and the all-even-n claim.
events.direction: Claims cases n = 2 and n = 4 of the statement; cuts toward the statement for those cases only.

events.what_happened: Hao Pan, arXiv:1306.2032 (9 Jun 2013): a conditional theorem. For k >= 3.5x10^6 and an admissible set H, for any m >= 1 the set {m(h_j - h_i)} contains at least one Polignac number.
events.delivers: Structural and conditional: some element of a set of multiples of tuple differences is a Polignac number, under the stated admissibility and size hypotheses. Not membership of every even n.
events.remains: Membership of every even n; the hypotheses are not shown to hold for the statement's purposes.
events.direction: Partial and conditional; cuts toward existence of some Polignac number in a set, not toward all even n.

events.what_happened: James Maynard, arXiv:1311.4600 (19 Nov 2013): unconditional H1 <= 600; for every m, H_m is finite (bounded intervals with m primes); under the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture, H1 <= 12 for consecutive primes. Published Annals of Mathematics 181 (2015) 383-413.
events.revisions: v3 28 Oct 2019 (typo corrections, per listing); journal version Annals 2015.
events.delivers: Unconditionally, some even gap <= 600 recurs infinitely often; for each m, bounded intervals contain m primes infinitely often. Conditional on Elliott-Halberstam, gap <= 12. No specific even n is identified.
events.remains: The all-even-n claim.
events.direction: Partial, toward bounded gaps; no named even n.

events.what_happened: Fred B. Holt and Helgi Rudd, arXiv:1402.1970 (9 Feb 2014; v2 15 Feb 2014): claim that for every even 2n the gap 2n occurs infinitely often through the stages of the Eratosthenes sieve.
events.delivers: A statement about the sieve's generators at each stage, not about primes. Discounted: an analogue of the conjecture for a different sequence.
events.remains: Everything for the primes.
events.direction: Analogue only: cuts toward the conjecture for the Eratosthenes-sieve sequence, not for primes.

events.what_happened: D.H.J. Polymath, 'Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes', arXiv:1407.4897 (v1 18 Jul 2014). Unconditional H1 <= 246; under the generalised Elliott-Halberstam conjecture H1 <= 6. Wikipedia reports the Polymath wiki gave n = 246 as of 14 April 2014, so the bound was public at least from that date. An earlier Polymath stage gave 4680 (2013, per secondary sources).
events.revisions: arXiv v1 18 Jul 2014 (79 pages; a minor fix to (117)); retrospective arXiv:1409.8361 (30 Sep 2014). Date above is the wiki 'as of' date, an upper bound on the first public write-up; the arXiv date is 2014-07-18.
events.delivers: Unconditionally some even gap <= 246 recurs infinitely often; conditionally on GEH, gap <= 6. No specific even n is identified beyond these bounds.
events.remains: The all-even-n claim.

The 2026 comment says it was reformatted with an expanded introduction and 'the ideas remain unchanged'.

events.what_happened: John K. Sellers, 'A step towards proving de Polignac's Conjecture', arXiv:2108.13834 (v1 27 Aug 2021; v2 13 Sep 2021; v3 13 Nov 2021; v4 16 Nov 2021). Conditional argument: for a consecutive pair in a set of numbers coprime to small primes with a given even gap, unboundedly many actual prime pairs with that gap. Proves the conjecture only for a range of known gaps; the full conjecture needs existence for every even gap. v4 adds a section proving existence of some gaps.

events.what_happened: Jason R. South, arXiv:2206.01179. v1 (31 May 2022, title 'An Algebraic Approach to the Goldbach Conjecture'): 'Once these theorems have been established Polignac's Conjecture will follow as a consequence.' v12 (31 Mar 2025, title 'A Proof of the Goldbach and Polignac Conjectures'): 'A proof of the Polignac Conjecture will then follow.' v13 (16 Feb 2026, title 'An Algebraic Approach to the Goldbach and Polignac Conjectures Using Mihailescu's Theorem and p-adic Analysis'): 'We then prove the Goldbach Difference Conjecture similarly, from which the Polignac Conjecture follows.' v14 (13 Aug 2026) and v16 (9 Sep 2026): title 'An Algebraic Approach to the Goldbach Conjecture'; the abstract no longer mentions Polignac (v14 and v16 read). The comments on v13 and v14 say 'significant simplifications made'.

events.what_happened: Giulio Morpurgo, 'On a Stricter Twin Primes Conjecture, and on the Polignac's Conjecture in general', arXiv:2210.15487 (v1 16 Oct 2022; v2 10 Mar 2023). Presents Polignac and the twin prime conjecture as unproven; proposes a stricter twin-prime conjecture; gives numerical predictions for ratios of Polignac solution counts for even M, checked for M up to 3000 and 30030.
events.delivers: Heuristics and numerics; no proof of anything in the statement.

events.what_happened: Julia Stadlmann, 'On primes in arithmetic progressions and bounded gaps between many primes', arXiv:2309.00425 (v1 1 Sep 2023; v3 22 Feb 2025). Exponent of distribution 1/2 + 1/40 for smooth moduli (Polymath had 1/2 + 7/300); gives liminf (p_{n+m} - p_n) = O(exp(3.8075 m)). The v3 comment says 'accepted for publication in Advances in Mathematics'; I did not verify the journal record.
events.revisions: v3 22 Feb 2025 (comment: accepted in Advances in Mathematics).
events.delivers: Bounded gaps for m-tuples of primes; no statement that any particular even n occurs infinitely often. Discounted as a neighbouring bounded-gap result, though it is the input to the 2026 Stadlmann work.
events.remains: All even n.
events.direction: Bounded-gap result for m-tuples; no statement for specific even n.

events.what_happened: Yuda Chen, Xiangjun Dai, Huixi Li, 'Some results on a conjecture of de Polignac about numbers of the form p + 2^k', arXiv:2402.06644 (1 Feb 2024). Improves an upper bound on the density of integers of the form p + 2^k (to about 0.4903).
events.delivers: Concerns de Polignac's odd-number conjecture on p + 2^k. A different problem sharing a namesake; settles nothing here.
events.remains: Everything in the statement.

events.what_happened: William D. Banks, 'Consecutive primes and IP sets', arXiv:2403.10637 (15 Mar 2024): proves that every IP set of even natural numbers contains infinitely many de Polignac numbers (m with p_{n+1} - p_n = m for infinitely many n).
events.delivers: Structural: within IP sets of even numbers, de Polignac numbers are plentiful. Does not show any given even n is a de Polignac number.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'Improved Short Gaps Between Primes' (cdn.openai.com PDF, dated 30 Aug 2026 per the Breakthrough Tracker; announced 3 Sep 2026 per tracker and an X post; a companion 'abridged chain of thought' PDF also exists). Claims liminf (p_{n+1} - p_n) <= 186 by proving DHL[40,2] and applying it to an admissible 40-tuple of diameter 186, using Polymath8a and Stadlmann's equidistribution estimates with extra factorisation conditions. The Lean development (github.com/openai/PrimeGaps186, opened) proves primeGapLiminf_le_186 conditional on three explicit input axioms: a rank-three hyper-Kloosterman bound of 3 (attributed to Deligne, as in Katz 1988), a rank-two correlation bound of 8p*sqrt(p) (Fouvry-Kowalski-Michel), and 104 outer, 45 inner and 3 cap numerical bounds checked by a Python-FLINT certificate outside Lean. The README says the formal proof 'verifies conditional proofs, not the inputs themselves'. The OpenAI PDF was not readable to me (binary); the paper's contents are from the repository and secondary trackers.
events.revisions: Companion 'abridged chain of thought' document (not read).
events.delivers: Conditionally (on three inputs, two of them cited literature estimates and one numerical): some even gap <= 186 recurs infinitely often. Does not single out any even n. Does not establish that every even n recurs. The twin-prime gap 2 is not established (tracker).
events.remains: Every even n, the statement as asked; and the bounded-gap statement itself, unless the three inputs are accepted.

disputes.summary: Stadlmann's 240 result (31 Aug 2026) is built on by Axiom's 212 (which says its analytic ideas come from Stadlmann) and by OpenAI's 186 (which cites her equidistribution estimates). A secondary report, not verified, says OpenAI announced a 240 proof on 2 Sep 2026 without citing Stadlmann. Stadlmann's own position on AI use is also reported only secondhand, and the report I opened for it does not contain that quote.

Jason South's arXiv:2206.01179 claimed Polignac's conjecture as a consequence of its Goldbach results in versions v1 to v13 (through 16 Feb 2026). From v14 (13 Aug 2026) the abstract no longer mentions Polignac. This is a change of claimed scope between versions, not a stated withdrawal.

summary: The problem's statement has not moved: no source I read proves that every even n is a prime gap infinitely often, and no accepted result settles any single even n beyond the bounded-gap family. The events are of three kinds. (a) Bounded-gap results, which are about a different quantity: the least gap H1 that recurs infinitely often, which the Polignac statement does not name. These run Maynard's 600 (published in Annals) and the Polymath 246 (a collaborative write-up), both pre-window, then Stadlmann 240 (arXiv 2608.31126, 31 Aug 2026, unconditional), Song and Yue 236 (ePrint 2026/1893, Sept 2026, unconditional per abstract), Charton et al. 212 (Axiom, 3 Sep 2026, preprint on the company site), and OpenAI 186 (preprint dated 30 Aug 2026, announced 3 Sep; conditional on three input axioms, with a Lean development that is sorry-free by the repository's comparator listing but does not prove the inputs). (b) Claimed proofs of the full statement, all unrefereed: Lynch (Zenodo, 25 Jan 2026; says RH is needed for the error term despite the 'Unconditional' title), the tower-sieve Zenodo record (19 Jun to 25 Aug 2026; claims to bypass the parity barrier, argument not read), Sankei et al. (MUSTIC 2024, online 2025; asserts the key step), Ting (J. Math. Research 2024; the same abstract claims RH), and South (dropped Polignac from the abstract in Aug 2026). (c) Claimed twin-prime (n = 2) or cousin (n = 4) cases, mostly from 2013 to 2019, none accepted; some were withdrawn or are unverified. The AI question is narrow. For OpenAI's 186 result the credit is to 'GPT-6 Astra', but the authors' own sentence is not quoted here: the PDF did not parse, the OpenAI page returned 403, and the only quote I have is Weijie Su's X post as relayed by an aggregator. For Axiom's 212 the only AI language I could read is 'formally verified by AxiomProver, relative to the existing literature' and 'human-AI collaboration'; it does not say AxiomProver produced the analytic argument, so I have left it out of ai.systems under §5.4, but that call is close. Axiom's 246 Lean library is formalisation only. Stadlmann's 240 shows no AI statement in the parts of the HTML I read, and the report that she disclaimed AI use is not in the article I opened. The public Wikipedia article still gives 246 (2014) as its current bound, although its footer shows an edit in October 2026. Close calls: (1) whether bounded-gap moves count as moving this problem, since the statement is about every even n and the H1 constant is a different quantity; (2) whether the 186 and 212 results should carry AI as load-bearing, which depends on the authors' own text I could not open; (3) whether the South v13 claim, which is in an earlier version, counts, since v14 dropped it without a stated reason.
competing_reading: On a reading that counts any movement in a quantity a statement touches, the Polignac statement is moved by every bounded-gap result, because each shows that some even gap recurs infinitely often and the set of Polignac numbers is non-empty by those bounds. On the stricter reading the statement asks about every even n, and a finite bound on H1 names no n, so none of 240, 236, 212 or 186 moves the question. For AI, the reading that AI is load-bearing for 186 rests on the credit to GPT-6 Astra, which I could only take from the tracker and an aggregator. The reading that AI is not load-bearing for 212 rests on the absence of any statement that AxiomProver produced the argument. If the OpenAI paper says the model found the idea, that is load-bearing under §5.4 whatever the Lean status.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The OpenAI 'Improved Short Gaps Between Primes' PDF text, its author list, and its acknowledgement of who produced the argument. (2) The Axiom 212 PDF text and its statement of AxiomProver's role. (3) The full texts of Stadlmann 2608.31126 and Song-Yue 2026/1893, including any AI disclosure. (4) Referee or expert reports on the 186, 212, 236 and 240 results, and any journal acceptance. (5) For the claimed full proofs (Lynch; tower sieve; Sankei; Ting; South v13), any expert review, any refereed acceptance, or an error identified in the key step. (6) Whether the arXiv v13 to v15 versions of South's paper contain a stated reason for dropping Polignac. (7) Whether the tower-sieve PDF and the Lynch code reproduce the stated claims.

Other gaps: Stadlmann's 240 is recorded as having no AI on the parts read, not on the whole paper; the 186 event's date uses the paper's own date, which I did not verify from the PDF; the 240-by-OpenAI event rests on secondary summaries that cite a source which does not contain it.
